routes.evidence: Published beta on Mt. Adams confirms three north-side routes (North Face of Northwest Ridge, North Lyman Glacier, Adams Glacier) share the Killen Creek approach to High Camp, and that a bivy exists on the moraine below the Adams Glacier icefall around 7,700 ft. The North Ridge itself is gained higher up past a small glacial lake on different ground than the moraine, so the moraine bivy is correctly a secondary/route option rather than the main camp.

Route descriptions place the jump-off for Burnt Boot Peak at the very end of the Middle Fork Snoqualmie road, at the Dutch Miller Gap trailhead — the same location as Hardscrabble Horse Camp. No other camp is documented for this peak.

The Dutch Miller Gap trail passes Pedro Camp then reaches Williams Lake beneath Bears Breast, directly below Iron Cap Mountain, matching it as the closer main camp; Hardscrabble Horse Camp several miles downstream is a staging/overflow camp for the whole zone, matching its route role. The hidden pins duplicate these two named camps, as the first researcher noted.

Goatshead Spire sits on the same Lemah massif reached by the standard Pete Lake / Lemah Meadows approach; no separate approach or camp is documented for the spire itself, so it plausibly shares the main camp.

Trip reports describe two distinct camping spots used by Lemah climbers: a meadow/campsite near the PCT/Lemah Creek junction (~3,600 ft, the 'Pete Lake and Lemah Meadows camps' entry) and a flat-topped boulder camp at the 4,800 ft meadow closer to the climb (the basin camp). Nothing found indicates one is clearly more used than the other, matching the first researcher's own uncertainty, so both stand as main.

Sources describe both a first-night camp at Waptus Lake (a long, ~16-mile summit day from there) and closer camps near the Waptus River bridge/Chief Creek ford for parties who want to shorten the push to the Summit Chief group — consistent with Waptus Lake as a route/staging camp and the closer Talus Basin as the main camp used to reach the peak.

Beta on the Ptarmigan Ridge approach to Baker's northeast side confirms Camp Kiser is a waypoint camp on the ridge, and that climbers continue on to camp at the Portals/Flats beyond it before the Park Glacier Headwall or Cockscomb — matching Park Glacier camp as the main camp and Camp Kiser as the route/staging camp.

Trip reports note parties camp at the end of the official Cougar Divide trail but that water is scarce or absent there by late summer, and that Deadhorse Creek — the drainage between Cougar Divide and Skyline Divide — is the nearby basin with water and shelter. This matches the Cougar Divide meadow camp as the on-route main camp and Deadhorse basin as the route-tier water/shelter fallback.

The first ascent account (Herrington/Wertkin) explicitly describes leaving the North Fork Bridge Creek trail before Grizzly Creek and bivying on an exposed bench below the technical climbing after a 5th-class pitch at dusk — directly confirming the bench bivy as the route's real camp. Fireweed, North Fork, and Walker Park camps are ordinary trail camps well downstream/short of that turnoff, consistent with their route/overflow role.

Multiple trip reports describe the 5,500 ft bivy below the slabs as the commonly used camp on this approach, and separately describe parties camping higher on the moraine/rubble at the Goode Glacier toe (6,400-6,800 ft) — supporting both as legitimate, commonly used main camps rather than one being a fallback. The hidden 'Lateral moraine camp' pin sits in the same 6,800 ft band as the Goode Glacier toe entry, consistent with it being a duplicate as already treated.

The documented Ptarmigan Traverse approach goes Cascade Pass to Cache Col, down to Kool-Aid Lake camp (6,120 ft), then across the Middle Cascade Glacier to the Spider-Formidable col (7,320 ft) directly below the Formidable Glacier and NE Face — matching Kool-Aid Lake and the col as the two real camps (first night and high camp) and Cache Col as a pass-through waypoint, not a camp.

All documented Magic Mountain routes from the Cascade Pass side (South Ridge, and the technical west-face lines) use Kool-Aid Lake as the base camp reached via Cache Col; no route description found uses Pelton Basin for a Magic Mountain approach, so Kool-Aid Lake stands as the main camp.

Graybeal Camp sits on the Brush Creek Trail directly below Indian Mountain, which rises over 4,100 ft above the Brush Creek valley in about a mile — consistent with Graybeal as the natural staging camp for the peak, with Hannegan, Boundary and US Cabin as camps further back along the Chilliwack/Hannegan approach.

Sources confirm Chicago Camp is where the maintained Elwha trail ends and cross-country travel into Elwha/Queets Basin begins, matching both as the last-camp/base pairing for a peak this deep in the Bailey Range interior. No documented standard camp specific to Dana was found, so I could not improve on the first researcher's own low-confidence placement; no change made without specific evidence.

Sources confirm Low Divide is the saddle base camp shared by Mount Seattle and Mount Christie climbs. I found no specific confirmation of which side (Elwha vs. Quinault) is used for the Noyes Basin line specifically, so the Elwha trail camps stay at route tier as the first researcher already hedged; no evidence to justify removing or promoting them.

Colchuck Lake is the documented base camp for the Colchuck/Dragontail group, but because Enchantments core-zone permits are extremely limited, sources confirm parties commonly camp at Eightmile/Bridge Creek campgrounds on Icicle Creek Road and do the approach as a long car-to-car day instead — supporting both as real, commonly-used main camps.

Witches Tower is reached over Aasgard Pass from the Colchuck side, and the same permit scarcity that pushes Colchuck/Dragontail parties to Icicle Creek Road camps applies here, supporting both Colchuck Lake and the Eightmile/Bridge Creek campgrounds as real options; no evidence found to favor one over the other or to confirm how often the tower is done car-to-car.

Trip reports describe a small bench camp reached by a gully scramble from the Chiwawa basin that is used as the base for 'storming' Fortress, matching the Chiwawa Basin bench as the main camp, with Phelps Creek Campground as the road-access staging camp lower down.
